title: parahebe raoulii subsp. maccaskillii
intro: Parahebe raoulii subsp. maccaskillii, commonly known as Raoul's hebe, is a flowering plant that belongs to the mint family (Lamiaceae) and is native to New Zealand. This plant is traditionally used in herbal medicine for its health benefits, which include reducing inflammation and relieving digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of Raoul's hebe are attributed to its antispasmodic, anti-inflammatory, and antacidal properties, which help to soothe and calm the body. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
